name: Alpbacher Seentour
kurzbeschreibung: The Alpbacher Seentour on the Kramsach lake plateau connects idyllic natural lakes such as Reintalersee, Krummsee, and Frauensee against the backdrop of the Rofan mountains.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Alpbacher Seentour – known locally as the Kramsach Lake Circuit – explores the scenic Kramsach lake plateau at the foot of the Rofan mountains. The classic circular walk covers approx. 6.8 kilometers with a gentle 72 meters of elevation gain (highest point at 585 m). Graded as easy, it is ideal as a half-day outing for nature enthusiasts and families.

Lakes & Landscape

Several notable bodies of water lie along the trail: Reintalersee is the plateau's largest lake and, with water temperatures up to 25 °C, one of the warmest swimming lakes in Tyrol. The tour also visits the protected Krummsee, the small water lily haven Buchsee, and the natural monument Frauensee in a quiet forest basin.

Visit & Getting There

The trails are freely accessible all year round; prime hiking season is April to November. Guests with the regional Alpbachtal Card can join the guided nature hike free of charge. Start and finish is in Kramsach village center (Volksschule car park). By car: Inntalautobahn A12, exit 32 Kramsach/Brixlegg. By public transport: ÖBB train to Brixlegg or Rattenberg-Kramsach, then VVT bus 621 to Kramsach Gemeindeamt.

Tips

The paved lakeside path around Reintalersee is fully wheelchair- and stroller-accessible. Bring swimwear on warm summer days to enjoy the bathing lawns at Reintalersee.
